newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Adtranz clear Pafawag sale.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Adtranz clear Pafawag sale.

text.p: The Polish privatisation ministry on Saturday signed an initial agreement with Adtranz, a joint venture of ABB group and Daimler-Benz AG, on selling it's large rolling-stock maker Pafawag SA, the ministry said in a statement.
Under the agreement, Adtranz would pay $3.7 million for a 75 percent stake in ailing Pafawag, bring modern technology there and invest $28.1 million over the next six years.
The agreement will become effective when Pafawag, based in the south-western city of Wroclaw, and the Polish State Railways (PKP) agree on a locomotive delivery programme.
Adtranz would then increase Pafawag's capital by $6 million and launch the production of a high-speed state-of-the-art locomotive, it said.
Pafawag's employment is to be maintained at the current level of 1,620 people.
For Adtranz, which has been in talks on the Pafawag acquisition for years, PKP purchase guarantees have always been the key condition for its investment.
The cash-strapped PKP has been reluctant to make a long-term purchase commitment.
Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said earlier this week that a tender of Pafawag sale could be annuled unless Adtranz approved the tentative deal.
Kaczmarek's portfolio is to be liquidated on October 1 under a cabinet reorganisation and some investors are uncertain how the privatisation policy will be implemented after that date.
